transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-04-15 10:00 PDT | Duration: ~42 minutes | Recording: yes
Attendees: Riley Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Singh (Axiom ML Lead), Carlos Rivera (PM), Lina Zhou (Data Scientist)
Shared links: eval spreadsheet (https://redwood.app/notes/AX-POC-evals), prompt set archive (https://files.axion-analytics.com/poc/prompts), security FAQ (shared in chat)

[00:00] Riley: Hey everyone, thanks for joining on a Tuesday, appreciate it. Quick roll call — Jordan, you on?
[00:05] Jordan: Yep, here. Ready to go.
[00:07] Maya: Here. Thanks, Riley.
[00:09] Carlos: On.
[00:10] Lina: Present.

[00:32] Riley: Cool. Agenda — quick recap of last week, go over the eval results we pushed to the spreadsheet, highlight any regressions, then agree on tuning (temp, system prompt tweaks), and next steps for guardrails. Sound good?
[00:40] Carlos: Yep. We're mainly focused on the 'abbrev expansion' and 'dosage normalization' failing cases.

[01:05] Jordan: Quick note — the SE-run includes three model variants: rw-v1-13b (float32), rw-v2-13b-8bit, and a smaller 7b we used for low-latency baseline. I put raw scoring (ROUGE-L / exact match-ish heuristics / human acceptability flags) in the sheet.
[01:25] Maya: I saw that, there are some weird flips where the 8-bit variant does better on short prompts but regresses on long-procedure expansions.

[02:00] Riley: Right, the reg flags are in the spreadsheet, but let's surface the big ones. Jordan, can you summarize top three regressions since last checkpoint?
[02:12] Jordan: Sure. One — prompt group A12 (abbrev expansion) dropped pass-rate from 82% to 64% on rw-v2-13b-8bit when we enabled the quantized kernel. Two — the safety/gate false-positive rate increased when we tightened the toxicity filter (some clinical shorthand flagged incorrectly). Three — latency variability on Dedicated config when sequence lengths spike — that's more infra but affects end-user timeout SLOs.
[02:48] Lina: For A12, many failures are predictable: the model outputs an expanded term but with the wrong units, e.g. 'mg' -> 'g' in rare cases.

[03:15] Maya: Are we sure it's quantization only? Could be an instruction-tuning artifact from the system message change we made last week. We changed the system message to be more conservative.
[03:30] Jordan: Good point — when we toggled system instruction 'prefer shorter expansions' that overlapped with the quantization changes; the regression coincides with both. I ran an ablation (sheet tab: A12-ablation). The 8bit + conservative system prompt combo had the worst delta. 8bit alone was -6%, conservative prompt alone -10%, together -22%.
[04:05] Carlos: So it's multiplicative. That suggests a guardrail or tuned prompt might be needed for that prompt class.

[04:40] Riley: Practical question — for the POC success metric you defined, you want >=80% pass rate on core prompt groups and <2% safety false-positive. Are those still the target?
[04:54] Maya: Yes, core groups — abbrev expansion, dosage normalization, patient summary concision. Safety false-positive should be under 2% for clinical shorthand.
[05:10] Jordan: On safety FP we saw it go to 3.6% after we added the tightened threshold; mostly because the filter rules match short strings like 'HIV+' and flagged them.
[05:25] Lina: Right, short clinical tokens are noisy. We prefer whitelist-first approach then fallback to classifier for long-form content.

[05:50] Riley: Noted. Jordan, any tuning knobs you'd recommend this week?
[05:57] Jordan: Several. One: revert to previous system prompt for A12 and add a prompt-level override (explicit instruction 'do not change units, only expand abbreviations') — prompt templates live in prompt set A. Two: run targeted temperature sweeps 0.0, 0.2 for deterministic vs. creative. Three: enable per-prompt KV cache warmup so the longer sequences hit cached attention states.
[06:30] Maya: On temperature sweeps — our QA team wants deterministic outputs for normalization tasks, but for summarization we want some variance to improve readability.
[06:41] Riley: We can set per-route defaults: 0.0 for normalization routes, 0.3 for summarization. Jordan can test both.
[06:55] Carlos: Any impact on cost with lower temps?
[06:58] Jordan: Minimal on token compute; determinism affects sampling but not throughput. The real cost is model size / quantization. 8bit reduces cost ~35% but caused the A12 drop.
[07:18] Lina: Could we use a hybrid routing approach — use 13b float for normalization and 8bit for fluffier summarization?
[07:27] Jordan: Yes, that's routing policy we demo'd; Redwood supports per-policy fallbacks. We can route by prompt tag. Slightly higher orchestration complexity but doable.

[07:55] Riley: Let's walk the spreadsheet. Jordan, open tab 'Summary-2025-04-14' (he references).
[08:03] Jordan: (screen share mentioned in call) OK — first chart shows per-prompt pass rate trend. You can see A12 dip around 2025-04-11. The hist shows most other groups stable.
[08:30] Maya: The 'patient summary' group drop is small but concerning because it's our most visible UX surface. Any notable errors?
[08:38] Jordan: Mainly verbosity — it repeats lab values and includes extra interpretation. That was triggered by an update to system prompt 'explain when in doubt'.
[08:52] Riley: So for patient summary we should nudge the system prompt to be concise and ask for 'bulleted summary, under 120 words'. Simple fix.
[09:05] Lina: Also add a guardrail that rejects outputs longer than 200 tokens server-side.
[09:12] Jordan: Redwood can do post-generation checks in the console via the 'response policy' — we can run a length check + token-level regex to ensure units preserved.
[09:25] Carlos: On length checks — will that add latency while we check server-side regex?
[09:29] Jordan: Negligible, it's done as a lightweight post-process. If it fails, we can auto-re-run with lower temperature or fall back to the floating-point model.
[09:45] Maya: Good. About the safety false positives — what's the mitigation path? Are we retraining a small classifier or adjusting thresholds?
[09:55] Jordan: Short-term: heuristic whitelist of common clinical shorthand and an allowlist in the safety pipeline. Medium term: we can upload a small labeled set and Redwood can host a fine-grained classifier — but that takes a 2-week model training cycle.
[10:18] Riley: For POC, whitelist + prompt-level instruction wins. Jordan: add a 'short-token whitelist' and we'll re-run safety metrics.

[10:40] Jordan: I also ran a human eval sample — 300 items randomly sampled from last week's traffic. Human acceptability went from 88% to 79% on the quantized build because of the A12 and verbosity issues.
[10:56] Maya: That drop is material. Is the majority the A12 subset?
[11:00] Jordan: Yes, A12 and some summarization duplicates.
[11:08] Lina: Can we do targeted instruction tuning? Like few-shot in the prompt with examples of correct expansion?
[11:14] Jordan: Absolutely. Prompt engineering immediate; instruction fine-tuning (LoRA) is an option but out of scope for this POC timeline.
[11:24] Carlos: For the few-shot, we need to ensure examples don't leak PHI. We'll give sanitized examples.
[11:30] Riley: Good catch. Use synthetic examples. Jordan, add 4-6 few-shot examples to the A12 prompt.
[11:36] Jordan: Will do.

[12:05] (timestamp shows Speaker 2 / Riley overlaps)
[12:10] Riley: On infra — Jordan, you mentioned latency variance when sequence length spikes on Dedicated. Any quick mitigations?
[12:18] Jordan: Two immediate things — configure pre-warming for longer sequences and increase the autoscaling threshold for the Dedicated pool. Also enable batch splitting to avoid one huge sequence blocking the queue.
[12:35] Maya: Budget-wise, how much autoscale padding do we need to hit 99th percentile SLO?
[12:40] Jordan: Based on current traffic and the worst-case spikes, ~20% additional burst capacity should handle 99.5th pct. Cost estimate in the sheet — ~+$1.8k/month for reserved burst but that's POC math.

[13:05] Carlos: Could routing to another region reduce latency?
[13:09] Jordan: Region round-trip helps but introduces data residency concerns. Axiom requires US data stay in US, so multi-region isn't an option currently.

[13:30] Lina: Anything on evaluation scoring — are we comfortable with the hybrid of automated heuristics + human labels?
[13:38] Jordan: For POC, yes. Automated heuristics for fast feedback (ROUGE-L, exact token match for normalization), and 10% human sampled to catch semantic errors and safety. We also added a 'regression alert' when pass-rate delta >10% for a prompt group.
[13:57] Riley: The regression alert threshold was triggered; can you show the alerts?
[14:02] Jordan: (mentions alert list) Yes, A12 popped on 4/11. I added a tag 'regression-critical'.

[14:20] Maya: How often does Redwood re-run the baseline when models change? We want reproducibility.
[14:27] Jordan: We snapshot model variant, kernel config, system prompt, and RNG seed for each run. The console stores the run metadata. We can re-run deterministically by using the saved seed and temperature 0.0.
[14:45] Lina: Good — include that snapshot id in the spreadsheet.

[15:05] Riley: Quick logistics — can Jordan try three targeted experiments this week: (A) revert system prompt + 4-shot examples; (B) keep system prompt but revert quantization; (C) hybrid routing where normalization uses float13b and summarization 8bit. Capture pass rates.
[15:20] Jordan: Yep, will schedule runs and push to tab 'A12-experiments'.

[15:45] Carlos: Also, we need a clear rollback plan if a change causes a new regression in production.
[15:51] Riley: Redwood's rollout supports canary and auto-fallback — we can configure a canary of 10% and automatic fallback to previous model if pass-rate drops >5% in 30 minutes.
[16:05] Maya: That should be in the runbook.

[16:20] Riley: On guardrails, besides whitelist and length checks, any other suggestions?
[16:28] Jordan: Add token-level unit regex enforcement (units must match allowed unit set), prompt-level instruction enforcement, and safety allowlist. Also, set up an evaluation rule that marks 'units mismatch' as a failing condition automatically.

[16:55] Lina: One more: add a 'confidence score' to outputs — the model-calculated logprobs aggregated — so downstream UI can show low-confidence flags for manual review.
[17:04] Jordan: We can add per-response avg-token-prob as a metadata field. UX can surface low confidence.

[17:25] Riley: Any additional blockers from Axiom side?
[17:30] Maya: We need the PII/PHI handling confirmation in writing and the SOC2 artifacts — Carlos will want to loop security.
[17:38] Riley: I'll send the SOC2 snapshot and the KMS/HSM integration doc today.

[18:00] Carlos: Also procurement asked for a simplified cost model showing POC vs projected prod costs.
[18:07] Riley: I'll include that in the follow-up email.

[18:30] (short pause, some cross-talk)

[19:00] Jordan: Quick note about metrics — I added a column 'human adverse' where labelers can mark 'hallucinated assertion' vs 'minor formatting'. That helps prioritize fixes.
[19:14] Lina: Good taxonomy.

[19:40] Riley: Let's capture next steps — (recap) Jordan runs the three experiments; Jordan adds whitelist + few-shot examples; Riley sends security & pricing; Lina uploads edge examples; Maya will review. Any objections?
[19:55] Maya: No objections.

[20:12] Carlos: Timeline okay — we expect to reconvene same time next week.
[20:16] Riley: Scheduled for 2025-04-22 10am. I'll send invite.

[20:40] (closing)
[20:45] Riley: Thanks all. We'll track in the shared sheet. Bye.
[20:51] Maya: Thanks.
[20:53] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript: transcription includes occasional mislabels, some short phrases transcribed as 'kv cash' instead of 'KV cache', and minor punctuation errors as typical for Fireflies exports. The spreadsheet referenced has tabs: Summary-2025-04-14, A12-ablation, A12-experiments.
